title: Expected insurance payout and an actuarial break-even premium
scenario_markdown: For a one-year policy, insurer payout L is $0 with probability 0.970, $1000 with probability 0.025, or $10000 with probability 0.005. A fixed annual premium is collected once. Ignore administration, commissions, investment income, capital costs and profit loading. Find the premium giving zero expected underwriting profit under these simplified assumptions.
assumptions: The payouts are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
No costs or revenue other than the stated payout and fixed premium are modeled.
Break-even refers to expected profit, not a guarantee on an individual policy.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is expected payout in dollars per policy? Select the value rounded to four decimal places.

options.hint_markdown: Do not average only the two positive payouts; include their probabilities.
Include the rare $10000 payout as well as the $1000 payout.

stages.prompt_markdown: Which premium gives zero expected underwriting profit in this model?

options.text_markdown: $75 per policy, because expected profit is premium minus expected payout.
$0, because the most likely payout is zero.
options.hint_markdown: Break-even depends on expected payout across all outcomes, not the modal payout.

options.text_markdown: $10000, because the premium must equal the largest possible claim to break even in expectation.
options.hint_markdown: Expected break-even is different from covering the worst outcome on each policy.

stages.explanation_markdown: For fixed premium c, $E[c-L]=c-E[L]$. Set c=75. Individual policies can make or lose money; a real insurer must also account for costs, capital, risk and loading outside this simplified model.
